::: {style="font-size: 150%;"}
# Comments
:::

## Comments [☆]{style="color: red;"}
- We assess $|\mathcal{A}_n^{{\mathscr I}^+}e^{i\omega_n \tau}|$ with a suitable normalisation. If $\mathcal{A}_n^{{\mathscr I}^+}$ is not numerically stable, then we are making (good looking) plots that change for each grid resolution.
- We need call "relative modal weight" the quantity 
$$ W_n(\tau)=\frac{\left\vert\mathcal{A}_n^{{\mathscr I}^+} e^{i\omega_n\tau}\right\vert}{\max_n \left\vert\mathcal{A}_n^{{\mathscr I}^+}e^{i\omega_n\tau}\right\vert},$$ 


In order to take into account the beating between eigenvalues of opposite real part, it is natural to evaluate
$$\sum_{\substack{\mathrm{Re}(\omega_n)\geq 0 \\ \mathrm{Im}(\omega_n)\geq 0}}\frac{\mathcal{A}_n^{{\mathscr I}^+}e^{i\omega_n\tau}+c.c.}{2}$$


We will consider
$$ W_n^{c.c.}(\tau)=\frac{\left\vert\frac{\mathcal{A}_n^{{\mathscr I}^+} e^{i\omega_n\tau}+c.c.}{2}\right\vert}{\max_n \left\vert\frac{\mathcal{A}_n^{{\mathscr I}^+} e^{i\omega_n\tau}+c.c.}{2}\right\vert},$$ 

$$ W_n^{c.c.,n.r.}(\tau)=\left\vert\frac{\mathcal{A}_n^{{\mathscr I}^+} e^{i\omega_n\tau}+c.c.}{2}\right\vert,$$

## Zerilli: $\ell=3$
- A mode sits at $\omega=40i$, its eigenfunction is very similar to the $\ell=2$ AS mode (it cancels at the horizon).
- Convergence test ? Difficult because the mode sits very high in the complex plane.

Typo in this animation: $a=0$, not $0.01$
